contradictions.title: Raw and calibrated customer sentiment differ
contradictions.description: The raw acoustic model classified the customer sentiment as 'Negative', while calibration changed it to 'Neutral/Mixed'.
contradictions.likely_explanation: Calibration reduced the influence of raw negative predictions because no strong negative or escalation indicators were found.
contradictions.recommended_action: Use the calibrated sentiment for operational decisions while retaining the raw prediction for auditability.

contradictions.title: Acoustic and transcript-based customer emotion assessments differ
contradictions.description: The raw acoustic model identified the customer's dominant emotion as 'sadness', while the transcript-based evaluation described the customer as 'calm'.
contradictions.likely_explanation: The acoustic emotion summarizes emotional signals across the full call, while the final text assessment may reflect the customer's resolved end state.
contradictions.recommended_action: Review the emotion trajectory and final call phase before using either emotion label as the sole operational decision.
